newsitem.title: VATICAN: U.S. Church presses Vatican on non-sexist wording.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Church presses Vatican on non-sexist wording.

text.p: Senior U.S. Roman Catholic Churchmen urged the Vatican on Friday to approve a revised English version of scripture readings which includes non-sexist language.

A Vatican statement said seven visiting U.S. cardinals had expressed their concern in meetings with Vatican officials that the book, known as the Lectionary and based on the New American Bible, be given the theological green light.
The Lectionary contains readings from the Bible used during Roman Catholic masses.
"The cardinals presented the (American Church's) concern that the revised New American Bible edition of the Lectionary of the Mass be approved as soon as possible," the statement said.
It said part of the discussion at the meeting focused on so-called inclusive language.
In 1994 the Vatican rejected part of the revised New American Bible for liturgical use because of what Church sources said were Vatican problems with inclusive language.
The new Lectionary tries to avoid exclusive language -- the use of the male pronoun and adjective for words that cover both sexes, such as "mankind" or "man".
Vatican officials have expressed concern in the past that omitting male pronouns can change the meaning of scripture in some cases.
A final review of the Lectionary's text would take place early next year between U.S. bishops and Vatican representatives.

The statement said the American cardinals and Vatican officials who took part in the meetings agreed that the norms used to reach agreement should reflect "fidelity to the sacred texts and the doctrine of the Church".
